Eligibility criteria
If you hold a Ukrainian driving licence and you are living in Great Britain (GB) on a Ukraine visa scheme, you can drive in Great Britain.
The length of time you can continue to drive depends on when you successfully applied for entry clearance or permission to stay in the United Kingdom.
Criteria for 36 month extension
You can drive in Great Britain for up to 3 years (36 months) after you became resident if you have or had permission to stay under:
the Ukraine Extension Scheme, which you applied for on or before 16 May 2024 and you have not applied for the Ukraine Permission Extension Scheme
the Homes for Ukraine Sponsorship Scheme (HFUS) which you applied for before 3pm on 19 February 2024 and you have not applied for the Ukraine Permission Extension Scheme (UPES)
the Homes for Ukraine Sponsorship Scheme, where the application was made on or after 3pm on 19 February 2024, and have either not applied for the Ukraine Permission Extension Scheme or, if granted leave under that scheme, have not applied for an extension of that leave
the Ukraine Family Scheme and you have not applied for the Ukraine Permission Extension Scheme
Criteria for 54 month extension
You can drive in Great Britain for up to 4 years and 6 months (54 months) after you became resident, if you have or had permission to stay under:
the Homes for Ukraine Sponsorship Scheme which you applied for before 3pm on 19 February 2024
the Ukraine Family Scheme
the Ukraine Extension Scheme which you applied for on or before 16 May 2024 – provided you became resident in Great Britain on or after 3 March 2022
You must also then apply to the Ukraine Permission Extension Scheme before your existing leave to remain in the UK expires. This refers to the initial application under the Ukraine Permission Extension Scheme, not an application to extend leave granted under that scheme.
You can continue to drive in Great Britain while your application for the Ukraine Permission Extension Scheme is being processed. If you withdraw your application or your application is not successful, your eligibility to drive ends at that time.
If your application is not processed after 18 months, the period that you can drive after you become resident will be capped at 4 years and 6 months.
Criteria for 60 month extension
You can drive in Great Britain for up to 5 years (60 months) after you became resident if all of the following apply:
you had permission to stay under the Homes for Ukraine Sponsorship Scheme which you applied for at or after 3pm on 19 February 2024
you have permission to stay under the Ukraine Permission Extension Scheme and you applied for that leave before the expiry of your Homes for Ukraine Sponsorship leave
you have applied for an extension of your Ukraine Permission Extension Scheme before the expiry of your initial Ukraine Permission Extension Scheme leave period
You can continue to drive in Great Britain while your application for the extension to your Ukraine Permission Extension Scheme is being processed.
If you withdraw your application or your application is not successful, your eligibility to drive in Great Britain ends at that time.
If your application is not processed after 24 months, the period that you can drive in Great Britain after you become resident will be capped at 5 years (60 months).
Criteria for 78 month extension
You can drive in GB for up to 6 years and 6 months (78 months) after becoming resident if any of the following applies to you:
you held an HFUS visa and applied for that visa before 3pm on 19 February 2024, you have permission to stay under the Ukraine Permission Extension Scheme (UPES), which you applied for before the expiry of your HFUS leave, and now apply for an extension of your UPES leave before the expiry of your initial UPES leave period
you held Ukraine Extension Scheme (UES) leave, which you applied for on or before 16 May 2024, became resident in Great Britain on or after 3 March 2022, you have permission to stay under UPES which you applied for before the expiry of your UES leave, and now apply for an extension of your UPES leave before the expiry of your initial UPES leave period
you held Ukraine Family Scheme (UFS) leave, you have permission to stay under UPES which you applied for before the expiry of your UFS leave, and now apply for an extension of your UPES leave before the expiry of your initial UPES leave period
you have never held leave under HFUS, UFS or UES, held leave of a type described in UKR 29.3(b) or (c) of the Appendix Ukraine Scheme to the Immigration Rules, you have permission to stay under UPES which you applied for before the expiry of that leave, and now apply for an extension of your UPES leave before the expiry of your initial UPES leave period
You can continue to drive in Great Britain while your application for the extension to your Ukraine Permission Extension Scheme is being processed. If you withdraw your application or your application is not successful, your eligibility to drive in Great Britain ends at that time.
If your application is not processed after 24 months, the period that you can drive in Great Britain after you become resident will be capped at 6 years and 6 months (78 months).
Vehicles you can drive
This applies to licences that permit the driving of:
cars up to 3,500kg
motorbikes and mopeds
Exchanging your Ukrainian driving licence for a GB driving licence
If you want to exchange your Ukrainian licence for a GB licence, you must do this within 5 years of becoming resident in Great Britain.
The extension to the period during which you can drive on your Ukrainian licence does not extend this 5-year exchange period.
You can use this tool to exchange your driving licence.
Your licence should arrive within 3 weeks if you apply online. It may take longer if the Driver and Vehicle Licensing Agency (DVLA) needs to make additional checks.
If you passed your driving test before 28 December 2021
You can only exchange your driving licence for a GB licence that allows you to drive automatic vehicles. You will need to take a driving test for manual cars to keep driving these vehicles.
If you passed your driving test on or after 28 December 2021
If your current licence allows you to drive manual cars, you can exchange it for a GB licence that allows you to continue driving manual cars.
Northern Ireland
If you live in Northern Ireland, different rules apply.
If you hold a valid Ukrainian driving licence, you may be able to drive on that licence for up to 3 years after becoming resident in Northern Ireland.
See the Northern Ireland guidance on exchanging your foreign driving licence for further information.

Exemption from vehicle tax and registration
If you have been issued a visa under one of the Ukraine visa schemes, you do not need to tax or register your Ukrainian plated vehicle in the UK.
This exemption only applies to the following personally imported vehicles (vehicles used for private or personal use) with Ukrainian number plates:
motorcycles
cars weighing up to 3,500kg
Your vehicle must remain registered in Ukraine to benefit from this exemption.
You must make sure that you have insurance to drive your vehicle in the UK.
Vehicle tax is also known as Vehicle Excise Duty (VED).
How long you can use this exemption
The exemption applies for up to the first 3 years (36 months) from your entry into the UK if you were:
issued a visa under the Ukraine Family Scheme, the Homes for Ukraine Sponsorship (HFUS) Scheme or the Ukraine Extension Scheme
initially granted an 18-month stay under the HFUS Scheme and were granted a further 18-month visa extension under the Ukraine Permission Extension (UPE) scheme
If you have an 18-month UPE scheme visa
You do not need to tax and register your vehicle for up to 4 years and 6 months (54 months) from the date you entered the UK if:
you were initially granted a 36-month stay under the Ukraine Family Scheme, the HFUS Scheme or the Ukraine Extension Scheme
following this, you were granted an 18-month visa under the UPE scheme
You will only be eligible for the extended exemption of up to 4 years and 6 months (54 months), if you applied for the UPE scheme before the expiry of your previous Ukrainian scheme visa.
You can continue to use this exemption while your UPE application is being considered. The exemption will no longer apply if your application is refused, withdrawn or rejected.
If your UPE application is not processed within 18 months, the exemption period is capped at 4 years and 6 months (54 months) from the date you entered the UK.
Further exemptions if you have a 24-month UPE scheme visa extension
If you receive a further 24-month extension under UPE, you may qualify for a longer exemption depending on the visa you were initially granted.
Up to 6 years and 6 months (78 months)
You qualify for this exemption if:
you were initially granted a 36 month visa under the Ukraine Family Scheme, the HFUS Scheme or the Ukraine Extension Scheme
following this, you successfully applied for the UPE scheme before the expiry of your previous Ukraine visa scheme leave and were granted a further 18-month visa
following that, you were granted a 24 month visa extension under the UPE scheme
Up to 5 years (60 months)
You qualify for this exemption if:
you were initially granted an 18 month visa under the HFUS Scheme
following this, you successfully applied for the UPE scheme before the expiry of your HFUS Scheme visa and were granted a further 18-month visa
following that, you were granted a 24 month visa extension under the UPE scheme
You will only be eligible for the extended exemption of up to 6 years and 6 months (78 months) or 5 years (60 months) if you applied for the 24-month extension to your UPE scheme visa before the expiry of your initial UPE scheme visa.
You can continue to use this exemption while your UPE extension application is being considered. The exemption will no longer apply if your application is refused, withdrawn or rejected.
If your UPE extension application is not processed within 24 months, the exemption period is capped at 6 years and 6 months (78 months) or 5 years (60 months) from the date you entered the UK.
MOT test
You may need to take your vehicle for an MOT test. This depends on the age of the vehicle.
An MOT test makes sure that your vehicle meets road safety and environmental standards.
You may need to make alterations to your vehicle to pass an MOT test.
Read more information on MOTs.
Vehicle safety
You are responsible for making sure your vehicle is always safe to drive (‘roadworthy’). A vehicle can be unsafe even if you have a current MOT certificate. There are penalties for driving a vehicle in a dangerous condition. Read more information on roadworthiness and penalties.
If you transfer to a different visa
You do not need to tax or register your vehicle for 3 years from when you entered the UK if either of the following applies:
you were issued a Ukraine scheme visa, but transferred to a different visa within 3 years, such as a Skilled Worker visa
you entered the UK through an alternative route to the Ukraine scheme visa and later transferred to a Ukraine scheme visa
This exemption will apply for up to 4 years and 6 months (54 months) from the date you entered the UK if you were initially granted a 36-month stay under the Ukraine Family Scheme, the HFUS Scheme or the Ukraine Extension Scheme and have been granted a further 18-month visa under the UPE scheme.
This exemption will apply up to either 5 years (60 months) or 6 years and 6 months (78 months) if you have been granted a 24-month extension under the UPE scheme.
If you stay in the UK longer than 3 years
If you stay in the UK for more than 3 years and are not eligible for the extended exemptions from tax and registration, you will need to tax and register your vehicle with DVLA and receive UK number plates.

You can no longer use the ‘UK Immigration: ID Check’ app to complete the identity verification stage of your Ukraine scheme visa application.
Find out how to apply for the Ukraine Family Scheme or Ukraine Sponsorship Scheme (Homes for Ukraine).
You can use the ‘UK Immigration: ID Check’ app to complete the identity verification stage of your application.
The app will:
check that your identity document is genuine
verify that the document belongs to you
You must use:
your biometric passport from an EU country, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway or Switzerland
your biometric British national (overseas) (BNO), Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR) or European Economic Area (EEA) passport if you’re applying for the BNO visa
your expired biometric residence permit (BRP) if your application route allows - you can use it for 18 months after the expiry date printed on the card
The app will only work once you start your application online at GOV.UK. When you get to the identity verification stage you will be told to open or download it.
This app is only available in English.
You cannot use this app if you are applying to the EU Settlement Scheme. You must download the ‘EU Exit: ID Document Check’ app instead.
Check if you can use the app on your phone
Android users
You will need:
Android 8.0 and above – you can find this in your settings
at least 135MB of storage space to install the app
to be connected to 3G, 4G, 5G or WiFi
NFC (Near-Field Communication) so the app can scan your document – you can find this in your settings. If you can use your phone to pay for things using contactless, this means it has NFC and you can use the app
Download the app from the Google Play Store.
iPhone users
The ‘UK Immigration: ID Check’ app is available for iPhone 7 and newer models.
You will need:
an iPhone 7, 7 Plus or newer
iOS 15 or later - to find the software version installed, go to Settings > General, then About
at least 120MB of storage space to install the app
to be connected to 3G, 4G, 5G or WiFi
Download the app from the App Store.
Whichever phone you use, the app will need access to the camera. If the app does not request access, enable it in your settings.
How to use the app
You must start your application and create your UK Visas and Immigration account online at GOV.UK before you use the app.
Using the QR code
A QR code is a black and white square barcode that connects the ‘UK Immigration: ID Check’ app to your application. You can find the QR code on the web page for your application when you select ‘Confirm your identity’. It does not appear in your identity document.
If you are completing all of your application on a smartphone, you will not need to scan a QR code.
QR code example:
An image of a QR code.
Scanning the QR code
Open the app and select ‘QR code’ when you are asked how you are connecting the app.
Hold your device in front of the code and move it closer until the code is recognised.
Using the connection code
If you cannot use the QR code, you can use a connection code instead.
Open the app and select ‘Connection code’ when you are asked how you are connecting to the app. You will be given a connection code that you will need to enter on the web page of your application.
Scan your document
Make sure your document can be read by the app. The following symbol shows that your document has a biometric chip and can be read by the app.
An image of an E-passport symbol.
Scanning a passport
Take a picture of the photo page of your passport using your phone’s camera. The full page must be inside the frame, including the 2 lines of numbers and letters at the bottom of the page. Make sure your phone camera is focused on the text on the page.
The app will prompt you to adjust your phone to make sure you capture your document correctly. These prompts will appear in a text box at the top of your screen.
Make sure you include the entire photo page in your picture.
'Scan your document' screen – make sure you include all the information in your photo
Try taking the photo of your document at arm’s length if you are having problems.
'Scan your document' – try taking the photo of your document at arm's length if you are having problems
Video: how to scan a passport biometric chip
Watch our video on how to scan a passport biometric chip.
Top tips: scan a passport biometric chip
Scanning a BRP
Take a picture of the back of the card using your phone’s camera. The full card must be inside the frame, including the 3 lines of numbers and letters at the bottom of the card.
The app will prompt you to adjust your phone to make sure you capture your document correctly. These prompts will appear in a text box at the top of your screen.
You’ll then be asked to take a picture of the front of the card.
Check your document’s information
Remove any cases or covers from your document and phone.
Select the ‘check now’ button in the app when you are ready to start checking your document.
Place the phone on top of your document when the app tells you to ‘check your document’s information’. If the volume on your phone is turned up, you will hear a beep when your document has been recognised.
Move your phone around the document until the app recognises it. The chip is located in different places in different documents.
For HKSAR passports you should place the phone on the back of your document.
'Check your document’s information' screen – move the phone around the document until the app recognises it
On a BRP the chip is located on the back of the card. Place your card down so that the side with the chip is facing up. On newer BRPs, the chip will not be visible. Place your phone on the card, making sure that the top of the phone covers the card without overlapping it.
When the app has successfully read the chip in your document, the screen will say ‘information checked’. Do not move the phone until this message appears and the check is complete.
If the app does not recognise your document, the check will time out and the screen will say ‘information not found’. If this happens, you should slowly move your phone around the document until the app recognises it.
If you are using a passport and you continue to have problems, place the phone on the reverse cover or the photo page.
If the app cannot read the chip
If the app cannot read the chip in your document, you can choose to confirm your identity another way.
If you choose to confirm your identity another way, you’ll need to book an appointment at a Visa Application Centre (VAC) or a UK Visa and Citizenship Application Services (UKVCAS) service point.
HKSAR passports with a document number starting with ‘K’ may have chips that are harder to read. If you scan your HKSAR passport but the app cannot read the chip, you can restart the ‘confirm identity’ task on the application dashboard and use another BNO or EEA passport with a biometric chip if you have one.
You can travel to the UK on a different passport as long as it’s valid.
Scan your face
The screen will flash as it scans your face. Hold your phone’s camera in front of your face until the scanning is complete.
You can skip this step and provide different evidence to prove your identity if a flashing light may cause you difficulties. To do this, go to the ‘Find out more’ menu and select ‘Skip this step’.
If you are 9 or younger, you will not be asked to scan your face.
Take a photo of yourself
You must:
be in even lighting, against a plain, light-coloured background
keep your head straight and look directly at the camera
have a neutral expression and make sure your eyes are open and visible
include your head, shoulders and upper body (you can extend your arms or ask someone to take the photo for you)
You must not:
have anything covering your face or eyes
wear a head covering (unless it is for religious or medical reasons)
have any shadows, objects or people behind you

Completing your application
Once you have confirmed your identity, you can complete the rest of the application either on that device or any smartphone, tablet, laptop or computer.
Once you have completed your application, you do not need to keep the app downloaded on your phone. If your application is successful, you can travel to the UK using your digital immigration status. You will not get a vignette (sticker) in your passport.
If you need help using the app
If you have problems using the app, for example scanning your chip or completing your application, you can contact UK Visas and Immigration for help.
Signing in to your account
If you need to sign in to your UK Visas and Immigration account, use the link in the email you received when you created your account.
